note: A mode drilled by its one colour note: hear it change, find it in two positions with the root and the 6th lit, then aim for it over the chords. The text says what to press and where to look; every target says which chord it lands on.

exercise.title: D Dorian: find the 6th
exercise.focus: D Dorian · positions with the root on the A and low E strings · Dm7-G7
exercise.why: Dorian differs from natural minor by one note, so practise that note.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the backing: Dm for eight bars, four in D natural minor, then four in D Dorian. Play the scale up and down along with the neck. The faded note is the one to leave out: B in the first half, B♭ in the second.
Position with the root on the A string

The note that changed is {{6}} (B): tap it on the neck to hear it. In this position {{1}} sits at the 5th fret of the A string. Play the position up and down, then play short phrases that pass through {{6}}.
Position with the root on the low E
The same mode one position up: {{1}} sits at the 10th fret of the low E string. Find each ringed {{6}} before you play, then play the position up and down.
Press Play below to start the backing, which switches between Dm7 and G7. Improvise in either position. Land on {{d}} when Dm7 comes round and on {{b}} when G7 comes round.
